vocabulary.meaning_en: the line where two pieces of cloth are sewn together
vocabulary.example: The seam of my shirt is broken.

vocabulary.meaning_en: smooth, with no visible joins or problems
vocabulary.example: The new system made the work seamless.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a helping verb used with a main verb (be, do, have, modals)
vocabulary.example: "Can" is an auxiliary verb in "I can swim".

vocabulary.meaning_en: when someone allows you to do something
vocabulary.example: You need permission to leave early.
There is a prohibition on smoking here.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the skill or power to do something
vocabulary.example: She has the ability to learn fast.

vocabulary.meaning_en: an opinion about what someone should do
vocabulary.example: My teacher gave me good advice.

vocabulary.meaning_en: something you must do or have; no choice
vocabulary.note_ar: حيلة التهجئة: c واحدة و s مزدوجة: n-e-c-e-s-s-i-t-y
vocabulary.note_en: Spelling trick: one c, two s's: n-e-c-e-s-s-i-t-y.

vocabulary.meaning_en: can (used in tenses where can is not possible)
vocabulary.example: I will be able to help you on Tuesday.

vocabulary.meaning_en: it is not allowed; absolutely no
should (a little stronger and more formal; the proper thing)
vocabulary.example: You ought to visit your grandmother.

vocabulary.note_ar: غالبًا: I've got to / gotta في الكلام
vocabulary.note_en: Often: I've got to; "gotta" in fast speech.
vocabulary.example: I've got to finish this today.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a bad result if you don't do something

fine_lines.title: can vs could vs may vs might (possibility)
fine_lines.explanation_ar: كلها للإمكانية بدرجات مختلفة: can قرابة 100%، could حوالي 60-70%، may حوالي 50%، might أقل.
fine_lines.explanation_en: All show possibility with different strength: can about 100%, could about 60-70%, may about 50%, might less.

examples.sentence: I can help you on Wednesday.
I could help you on Wednesday.
I may help you on Wednesday.
I might help you, but I'm not sure.

fine_lines.title: should vs ought to vs had better (advice)
fine_lines.explanation_ar: should: نصيحة الأصدقاء وتترك لك الخيار. ought to: أقوى وأكثر رسمية، مثل نصيحة الأب (السلوك الصحيح). had better: الأقوى، معها عاقبة إن لم تفعل (مثل المعلم).
fine_lines.explanation_en: should: a friend's advice; you have a choice. ought to: stronger, more formal, like a parent (the proper way). had better: strongest; there is a consequence if you don't (like a teacher).

examples.sentence: Friend: You should study if you want to pass.
Father: You ought to study if you want to go to university.
Teacher: You had better study, or you will fail.

fine_lines.title: can vs be able to
fine_lines.explanation_ar: can للحاضر و could للماضي. نستخدم be able to في الأزمنة الأخرى (المستقبل، التام، بعد فعل ناقص آخر).
fine_lines.explanation_en: Can is present, could is past. Use be able to in other forms (future, perfect, after another modal).

examples.sentence: I have been able to swim since I was six. / I will be able to come tomorrow.

expressions.example: May I come in? Yes, you may.
Can you swim? Yes, I can.
You must not use your phone during the exam.
Sorry, I've got to go. My class starts soon.

expressions.meaning_en: Formal advice about the proper thing to do.
expressions.example: You ought to thank your teacher.

grammar.title: SEAM: four jobs of modals
grammar.explanation_ar: طريقة SEAM تجمع وظائف الأفعال الناقصة: S = التعبير عن التفضيلات (State preferences)، E = التعبير عن PAN (Express PAN)، A = الطلب (Ask for a pass)، M = تقديم الاقتراحات (Make suggestions). هذا الدرس عن E.
grammar.explanation_en: The SEAM method groups what modals do: S = State preferences, E = Express PAN, A = Ask (for a pass), M = Make suggestions. This lesson is about E.
examples: E = Express PAN: possibility, ability, necessity.

grammar.title: P: Possibility, Permission, Prohibition
grammar.explanation_ar: الإمكانية: can, could, will/would be able to, may, might. الإذن (التعبير عنه وليس طلبه): You can / You may. المنع: must not.
grammar.explanation_en: Possibility: can, could, will/would be able to, may, might. Permission (giving it, not asking): You can / You may. Prohibition: must not.
examples: I could help you next week. (possibility)
You may go to the party. (permission)
You must not go out tonight. (prohibition)

grammar.title: A: Ability and Advice
grammar.explanation_ar: القدرة: can (حاضر/مستقبل)، could (قدرة عامة في الماضي)، be able to (لباقي الأزمنة). النصيحة: should (خيار)، ought to (أقوى ورسمي)، had better (مع عاقبة).
grammar.explanation_en: Ability: can (present/future), could (general ability in the past), be able to (other forms). Advice: should (choice), ought to (stronger, formal), had better (with a consequence).
examples: When I was young, I could run very fast.
You ought to respect your elders.
You had better hurry, or you'll be late.

grammar.title: N: Necessity
grammar.explanation_ar: الضرورة (لا خيار لديك): have to، have got to، must.
grammar.explanation_en: Necessity (no choice): have to, have got to, must.
examples: I have to renew my passport.

grammar.title: Can and could: present and past; will/would be able to
grammar.explanation_ar: could هي ماضي can، و would be able to هي ماضي will be able to. لا نقول have can؛ نقول have been able to.
grammar.explanation_en: Could is the past of can; would be able to is the past of will be able to. We don't say "have can"; we say "have been able to".
examples: I can help you. / I could help you yesterday.
I have been able to read since I was four.

questions.question: In PAN, what does N stand for?
Which is the past of "can" for general ability?
questions.explanation_en: Could is the past of can for general ability.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
choices: I have able to help you.
I have been able to help you.
questions.explanation_ar: في التام نستخدم been able to.
questions.explanation_en: In the perfect tense use been able to.

questions.question: Teacher: "You ___ study, or you will fail." (consequence)
questions.explanation_en: Had better = advice with a consequence.

questions.question: Which advice word is more formal, like a parent speaking?
questions.explanation_en: Ought to is stronger and more formal.

questions.question: "Yes, you may go." This sentence expresses ___.
Which group shows necessity?
choices: have to, have got to, must
questions.explanation_ar: الضرورة: have to, have got to, must.
questions.explanation_en: Necessity: have to, have got to, must.

questions.question: What does "seam" mean?
choices: the line that joins two pieces of cloth
questions.explanation_en: A seam joins two pieces of cloth.

questions.question: Spell the word correctly.
questions.explanation_ar: c واحدة و s مزدوجة: necessity.
